reason: The bone window has spaces awaiting mineral, so adding it directly addresses the strengthening goal.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the living bone framework.

alternatives.reason: The cells also have a clear place to develop, but I can strengthen the bones first.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the joint able to move. Next I can build a muscle at one of the tendon attachments.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the mineral fill the spaces without hardening the joint.
reason: The front attachments have a space for muscle cells, so they are a clear place to start building a muscle.
expectation: The cells should form a muscle between the front tendons.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need a muscle; either side seems like a reasonable starting point.

effect: The front cells formed a biceps that bends the elbow. The back attachments still need a muscle.
reaction: The arrows made the connection between the muscle's position and bending clear.
reason: The back attachments are the remaining space for building a muscle on the opposite side.
expectation: The cells should form a muscle behind the elbow that pulls in the opposite direction.

effect: The back cells formed a triceps that straightens the elbow. Together with the biceps, it shows how attachments determine the direction of movement.
reaction: The contrast between the two muscles made their jobs clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile because the arrows connected their positions to bending and straightening the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cells to the second set of attachments was somewhat repetitive, though comparing the result with the first muscle made the repetition useful.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could make muscles that move the elbow in opposite directions because of where they attach.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the mineral had a visible space in the bone, and both tendon attachment areas had spaces for muscle.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because building the arm made the connection between structure and movement easy to follow, and I would be curious to see another body system built this way.
